artboards.title: App — what to do about it

annotations.text:
PICK ONE — then the Screens page gets rebuilt in it.

All three keep the red / yellow / green meanings from lib.js exactly: green = Star, red = Needs Attention / Retention Risk, yellow = Watch / Monitor. Only the hues are tuned per direction.

Each carries its own trade-off at the bottom. B is currently applied to the Screens page — not a verdict, just the one that had to be built out.

The full set, drawn in Direction B.

Three things changed beyond paint:
1. The answer leads. Grids and counts come first; loading data drops to a secondary action. Today the upload panel outranks the charts a manager came to read.
2. The report groups people by finding instead of giving each person a full-width card. Ten people used to mean ten stacked cards.
3. No emoji. The 🚨 / 🔑 headers become drawn icons and typographic labels — that was the main thing reading consumer-grade.

Copy is drafted, not final.
Landing keeps the free/paid split you shipped: this is the FREE state. The $49-later line stays in the hero rather than the footer, so nobody can miss it.
